title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + regional failover hysteresis to prevent thrashing
author: Ravi Patel
description: Motivation: Over the past 36 hours we observed repeated regional failover cycles (thrashing) driven by the SLO enforcer's aggressive backoff and immediate failover policy. This caused elevated error rates and increased token costs as the fleet repeatedly switched regions under transient congestion. Summary: This hotfix reduces failover-induced thrashing by making three coordinated changes to the SLO enforcer: (1) implement a hysteresis window before regional failover is triggered, (2) increase the minimum backoff and add smoothing across consecutive enforcement decisions, and (3) add telemetry and an integration test that reproduces the thrashing pattern. The changes are intentionally conservative to avoid increasing customer-visible latency while preventing oscillation under flapping signals. Behavioral changes: default backoff_min increased from 5s to 15s; backoff smoothing factor applied (exponential moving average on outage score) with a tunable alpha (default 0.4); regional failover now requires the outage score to be above threshold for two consecutive enforcement ticks (configurable via SLO_ENFORCER_FAILOVER_CONSECUTIVE=2). The PR also adds a small jitter and caps the failover rate to 1 region switch per 60s per tenant. Testing & rollout: unit + integration tests added; added an end-to-end canary that reproduces rapid transient congestion to ensure the enforcer remains stable. Rollout plan: staged rollout to dedicated staging and two customer-facing regions for 24h canary, then gradual global rollout. Notes: This is a hotfix cherry-picked against main and will be backported to release/2026-02 next. Related Linear tasks listed below.
